Title: Create a new order and verify the generated order ID follows the expected format and QR code is retrievable
Section: Order Management - Order ID Generation and QR Code
Preconditions: A shop with ID 1 exists in the system
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/orders with the payload in testData. 2. Note the orderId from the response. 3. Send a GET request to /api/orders/{orderId}/qrcode using the orderId from step 2.

Test Data: {
  "shopId": 1,
  "customerName": "John Doe",
  "customerPhone": "5551234567",
  "customerGender": "male",
  "orderGender": "male",
  "totalAmount": 2000.00,
  "paidAmount": 500.00,
  "dueAmount": 1500.00,
  "orderDate": "2023-10-01",
  "trialDate": "2023-10-05",
  "deliveryDate": "2023-10-15",
  "urgent": false,
  "items": [
    {
      "itemId": 1,
      "quantity": 1,
      "photoUrl": "http://example.com/photo1.jpg",
      "measurementGroups": [
        {
          "quantity": 1,
          "photoUrl": "http://example.com/measurement1.jpg",
          "urgent": false,
          "measurements": [
            {
              "nameEn": "Chest",
              "nameBn": "বুক",
              "unit": "inches",
              "type": "NUMBER",
              "value": "40"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
Expected Result: 1. HTTP 200 OK response with a JSON body containing: {"status": "success", "message": "Order created successfully", "data": {"orderId": "1-20231001-0001", "shopName": "<shop name>", "customerName": "John Doe", "totalAmount": 2000.00}}. 2. HTTP 200 OK response with a JSON body containing: {"qrCode": "data:image/png;base64,<base64-encoded-string>"}

Title: Verify that QR code generation for an order enforces proper authorization (insecure direct object reference) - unauthorized user cannot generate QR code for another user's order
Preconditions: Two users exist: User A (authorized for order 1001) and User B (not authorized for order 1001). Order 1001 exists and belongs to User A.
Steps: 1. Authenticate as User B. 2. Send a GET request to /api/orders/1001/qrcode.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 403 (Forbidden) or 404 (Not Found), and the response body contains a generic error message (e.g., 'Order not found' or 'Access denied'). No QR code or order details are returned.

Title: Verify that QR code generation for a non-existent order returns a generic error message without exposing system details
Preconditions: No order exists with ID 999999.
Steps: 1. Authenticate as a valid user. 2. Send a GET request to /api/orders/999999/qrcode.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 404 (Not Found) and a response body containing 'error: Order not found with ID: 999999'. No stack traces, database errors, or internal system details are exposed.

Title: Verify that QR code generation response does not expose sensitive system details in error messages
Preconditions: An order exists with ID 1001, but the QR code generation service is intentionally broken (e.g., by mocking a failure).
Steps: 1. Authenticate as a valid user. 2. Send a GET request to /api/orders/1001/qrcode.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 500 (Internal Server Error) and a response body containing 'error: An error occurred while generating the QR code'. No stack traces, database errors, or internal system details (e.g., exception class names) are exposed.

Title: Verify that QR code contains only authorized order data and no sensitive internal details
Preconditions: An order exists with ID 1001, containing customer name, shop name, total amount, due amount, delivery date, and items with measurement groups.
Steps: 1. Authenticate as a valid user. 2. Send a GET request to /api/orders/1001/qrcode. 3. Decode the Base64 QR code image and inspect the embedded JSON data.
Expected Result: The decoded QR code contains only the following fields: orderId, customerName, shopName, totalAmount, dueAmount, deliveryDate, and items (with group, itemName, and deliveryDate). No internal IDs (e.g., database IDs), Bengali names, or other unauthorized fields are exposed.

Title: Verify that order ID generation does not expose internal shop ID or sequence logic in responses
Preconditions: A shop exists with ID 50, and no orders exist for today.
Steps:
1. Authenticate as a valid user. 2. Send a POST request to /api/orders with a valid OrderRequest payload for shop ID 50. 3. Inspect the response body for the order ID.

Test Data: {"shopId": 50, "customerName": "John Doe", "customerPhone": "1234567890", "customerGender": "MALE", "orderGender": "MALE", "totalAmount": 1000, "paidAmount": 500, "dueAmount": 500, "orderDate": "2023-10-01", "trialDate": "2023-10-05", "deliveryDate": "2023-10-10", "urgent": false, "items": []}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 200 (OK) and a response body containing the order details, including an orderId in the format '50-20231001-0001'. The orderId does not expose internal logic or raw database IDs beyond the shop ID and date.

Title: Verify that order ID is exposed in order responses and summaries without leaking internal database IDs
Preconditions: An order exists with ID 1001 and orderId '50-20231001-0001'.
Steps: 1. Authenticate as a valid user. 2. Send a GET request to /api/orders/1001. 3. Inspect the response body for the orderId field. 4. Send a GET request to /api/orders/shop/50?page=0&limit=10. 5. Inspect the response body for the orderId field in the order summaries.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 200 (OK) for both requests. The response bodies contain the orderId field (e.g., '50-20231001-0001') but do not expose the internal database ID (e.g., 1001) in any field other than 'id' (which is expected).

Title: Verify that QR code generation enforces rate limiting to prevent abuse
Preconditions: An order exists with ID 1001, and the user is authorized to access it.
Steps: 1. Authenticate as a valid user. 2. Send 10 GET requests to /api/orders/1001/qrcode in rapid succession (within 1 second).
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 200 (OK) for the first few requests, then starts responding with HTTP status 429 (Too Many Requests) and a response body containing 'error: Too many requests. Please try again later.' for subsequent requests.
